source: RicksClips3000 era C (29 explainers, 6 Oct - 13 Nov 2026), studied 2026-11-15
hook_formula: Third-person absurd action with an object and stakes, past tense, 8-16 words: 'He [did insane thing] [while/because stakes]'
Second-person rule: 'If you X, you'd Y' / 'Imagine you're...' (use for what-ifs and how-things-work)

beat_template.purpose: the moment that only makes sense at the end; first frame shows the act
present tense, place, stakes, an everyman with a name or a job; often opened by 'You see,'
someone mocks the hero with a meme-able one-line quip (main comedy slot)
3-5 steps with numbers that grow or shrink; time passing shown by light
narrator or a character asks the viewer's question out loud
'You see,' + an everyday analogy with its own mini-scene; the real fact
ironic reversal, ideally the doubter destroyed by their own choice; spectacle; end mid-motion on the last word so it loops

pacing_targets.voice: no speed-up, no pause trimming; write short sentences instead

visual_rules: illustrate every line literally, especially figures of speech
light tracks time and mood: day, golden, night-blue for danger, warm interior for the reveal
1-2 epic scale wides per video, everything else CU/MS
analogy gets its own mini-set (top-down insert, diagram, other location)
props with readable text carry jokes and callbacks (counters, signs, tins, newspapers)
ending is a physical spectacle on the final word
OUR ADD: background chaos and second-watch gags nobody acknowledges
caption_rules: 1 word per card (2-3 max), white bold, black outline, at 60-74 % of the height, hard swap on each word
OUR RULE: 2-3 words with yellow keywords is allowed (rulebook)
sound_rules: voice from frame 1, no intro or outro
music and SFX bed about 5-10 dB under the voice, heavily compressed, -14 LUFS
SFX on every physical event; a music sting on the reversal
reusable_for: what-if second person with a closing choice
anti_patterns: pure explainer with no protagonist (0.14-0.32M vs a 9.6M median)
sci-fi what-if premise recaps without a trick (20-40K in era A)
